from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Compare 3D surface area to 2D shadow area.",
            "Shadows capture only the sphere's cross-section.",
            "Spinning the sphere keeps the shadow circular.",
            "Shadow area is always pi r squared.",
            "Surface area is four times the shadow area."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Projection Logic", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define objects
        sphere = Sphere(radius=1.0, color=BLUE).set_opacity(0.5)
        plane = Rectangle(width=2, height=0.1, color=WHITE).rotate(PI/2)
        center_dot = Dot(color=RED)
        
        # Grid positioning
        self.place_at_grid(sphere, "C3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(plane, "E3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Animations
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(FadeIn(sphere), FadeIn(plane))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFCC00")
        ray = Line(start=sphere.get_center(), end=plane.get_center(), color="#00FF00")
        self.play(Create(ray))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.play(Rotate(sphere, angle=PI, axis=RIGHT))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#00FF00")
        p_prime = Dot(point=plane.get_center(), color="#FFCC00")
        self.play(FadeIn(p_prime))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FF6600")
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Application", [
            "The sphere's surface is 4 times its shadow.",
            "This 4 to 1 ratio is constant.",
            "This ratio is critical for heat and light."
        ])
        
        # Define objects
        sphere = Sphere(radius=1, color=BLUE).set_opacity(0.5)
        circle = Circle(radius=1, color=YELLOW).set_stroke(width=4)
        
        # Initial positions
        self.place_at_grid(sphere, "B3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(circle, "E3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.play(Create(sphere), Create(circle))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        # Show projection logic
        projection_rays = VGroup(*[Line(sphere.get_center() + RIGHT * 0.5, circle.get_center() + RIGHT * 0.5, color=GREEN).set_opacity(0.3) for i in range(10)])
        self.play(FadeIn(projection_rays))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(projection_rays))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(sphere), FadeOut(circle))
        conclusion = Text("Conclusion", font_size=40, color=WHITE)
        self.add(conclusion)
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Geometry of Light: Sphere Surface Area and Its Projected Shadow
outline.target_audience: High school geometry or physics students

sections.title: Introduction & Prerequisites (1 minute)
sections.content: Briefly review the area of a circle (πr²) and the concept of a sphere. Establish the 'Parallel Light Assumption'—where light rays travel in straight, parallel lines to create a perfect circular shadow of a sphere.
sections.example: An orange held under a bright, distant desk lamp projecting a crisp shadow on a table.

sections.title: Conceptualizing the Sphere Surface (1.5 minutes)
sections.content: Introduce the formula for the surface area of a sphere (A = 4πr²). Visualize this by 'unwrapping' the sphere. Use an animation showing four identical flat circles (each πr²) being mapped onto the curved surface of the sphere to demonstrate why the total area equals 4πr².
sections.example: Imagine a hollow sphere made of play-dough; if we flatten its surface, it perfectly covers exactly four circles of the same radius as the sphere.

sections.title: The Projection Logic (1.5 minutes)
sections.content: Compare the 3D surface area (4πr²) to the 2D projected shadow area (πr²). Highlight that the shadow captures only the cross-section. Use an animation of a sphere spinning; note that regardless of rotation, the shadow remains a circle of area πr².
sections.example: A robotic probe in space detecting a planet. The sensor 'sees' only the circular shadow (πr²), while the actual surface area it must traverse is four times larger (4πr²).

sections.title: Summary & Application (1 minute)
sections.content: Synthesize the 4:1 ratio. Emphasize that the sphere's surface is 4 times the area of its shadow. Conclude with the importance of this factor in light absorption (solar panels on spheres) or heat radiation.
sections.example: Calculations for a spherical heat-shielding satellite: Understanding that to protect the whole surface, one must account for 4x the energy intercepted by its cross-sectional shadow.
